label: HTTP Request
description: Make an outbound HTTP request (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, JSON body, custom headers). Only no answer (unreachable host, dropped connection, unreadable body) is a failure; an error status (404, 500) succeeds with `status` and `ok` carrying it. A text response comes out on `body`: a JSON object as a dict, anything else (array, scalar, non-JSON text) as its raw text. A response whose type is not text (an image, a PDF, a zip), or a text one over 100 KB (the most a wire carries), comes out whole on `file` instead: wire `file` when a response can be that big. For an API key, pick a `connection` rather than writing it in `headers`.

fields.name: value
fields.label: Header value
fields.placeholder: Bearer sk-..., or the bare key

steps: Name the header the API reads its key from (`Authorization` for most, `X-Api-Key` for some).
Paste the header's whole value, with its prefix when the API wants one (`Bearer sk-...`).

inputs.name: connection
inputs.label: Connection
inputs.description: Optional: a key the request carries in the header the connection names. Leave unpicked for an API that takes bare calls.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The JSON object sent as the request's body. A secret in it (a token for the API) is revealed into the request where the type of what is wired here declares it, like `{ token: Secret[String] }`, and stays a marker on the run's record; a secret inside a body left as a `JsonDict` fails the node.

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Extra request headers. A secret value (a caller's `credentials.authorization`) is revealed into the request it sends, and stays a marker on the run's record.

outputs.name: body
outputs.description: A text response up to 100 KB, held to the type declared here: a JSON list or object the type takes comes out as itself (an object by default, a list or an object with `-> (body: Json)`), anything else as its raw text while the type takes text, and a type that takes no text (a record, `List[...]`, `Number`) gets the parsed JSON, checked against it. Absent when the response came out on `file`; with `file` unwired, a bigger text response fails the node instead.

outputs.name: file
outputs.description: A response whose type is not text (or that names no type and does not read as text), or a text one over 100 KB, stored whole. Absent for a text response that fits `body`.

then.message: HttpRequest '{id}' has a `url` that is not a web address. Start it with http:// or https://.
